#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=Tony_DPRV
#SBATCH --account=BYRNE-SL3-GPU
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --mail-type=NONE
#SBATCH --partition=ampere

# Set the working directory to the submission directory
cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR"

# Environment setup
. /etc/profile.d/modules.sh
module purge
module load rhel8/default-amp
source /usr/local/software/archive/linux-scientific7-x86_64/gcc-9/miniconda3-4.7.12.1-rmuek6r3f6p3v6fdj7o2klyzta3qhslh/bin/activate /home/ty308/.conda/envs/RAVQA2

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

# Define log files
LOG="/home/ty308/rds/hpc-work/myvqa/logs/logfile.$SLURM_JOB_ID.log"
ERR="/home/ty308/rds/hpc-work/myvqa/logs/to/errorfile.$SLURM_JOB_ID.err"

# Logging initial job information
echo -e "JobID: $SLURM_JOB_ID\n======" > "$LOG"
echo "Time: $(date)" >> "$LOG"
echo "Running on master node: $(hostname)" >> "$LOG"
echo "Current directory: $(pwd)" >> "$LOG"

if [ "$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST" ]; then
    # Site-specific: Create a machine file
    export NODEFILE=$(generate_pbs_nodefile)
    cat $NODEFILE | uniq > machine.file.$SLURM_JOB_ID
    echo -e "\nNodes allocated:\n================" >> "$LOG"
    echo $(cat machine.file.$SLURM_JOB_ID | sed -e 's/\..*$//g') >> "$LOG"
fi

echo -e "\nnumtasks=$SLURM_NTASKS, numnodes=$SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES (OMP_NUM_THREADS=$OMP_NUM_THREADS)" >> "$LOG"

# Define the application and its options
application="python src/tools/prepare_faiss_index.py"
options="--csv_path /home/ty308/rds/rds-cvnlp-hirYTW1FQIw/shared_space/vqa_data/KBVQA_data/ok-vqa/pre-extracted_features/passages/okvqa_full_corpus_title.csv \
    --output_dir /home/ty308/rds/hpc-work/data/ok-vqa/pre-extracted_features/faiss/ok-vqa-passages-full-new-framework \
    --dpr_ctx_encoder_model_name /home/ty308/rds/hpc-work/myvqa/Experiments/V_DPR/train/saved_model/epoch5/item_encoder \
    --dpr_ctx_encoder_tokenizer_name /home/ty308/rds/hpc-work/myvqa/Experiments/V_DPR/train/saved_model/epoch5/item_encoder_tokenizer"

CMD="$application $options"

# Log the command to be executed
echo -e "\nExecuting command:\n==================\n$CMD\n" >> "$LOG"

# Execute the application
eval $CMD

issues: The script calls a function `generate_pbs_nodefile`, which appears to be a leftover from a PBS/Torque job scheduler. This command is not standard in Slurm and will likely cause a 'command not found' error unless it is a custom, site-specific function.

The use of `eval $CMD` is strongly discouraged. It can be a security risk and can lead to unexpected parsing errors if filenames or paths contain spaces or special characters. It is safer to execute the command directly.

The script defines an error log file variable `ERR` but never uses it to redirect the standard error of the main `python` command. Any errors from the application will go to the standard Slurm output file, not the specified error file.
The path for the defined error log, `.../myvqa/logs/to/errorfile...`, may contain a typo ('to'). If this directory does not exist, the script will fail when it tries to create the log file.
The script does not use `set -e`. If any command before the main application fails (e.g., `module load` or `source activate`), the script will continue to run, leading to a confusing failure state.
